nonBlockingIssues.description: Code duplication in lib.rs: proxy stats recording block is copy-pasted between validate_emails_bulk and revalidate_emails_bulk. Should be extracted to a shared helper function.
Stats recording acquires write lock on settings after validation but before returning results, adding latency to every validation call. Acceptable at current scale.
recordProxySuccess and recordProxyFailure callbacks have empty dependency arrays [] in use-settings.ts, creating stale closures. Mitigated by getProxyFromStorage() reading latest state.
New proxies start with 100% success rate (0 attempts) making them appear 'Healthy'. Reasonable optimistic default but worth documenting.
bypass_cooldown resets both cooldown and bad status (consecutive_failures = 0). This means bypass achieves the same effect as a success for VAL-HLT-006 (failure counter reset).
pseudo_random() uses SystemTime::now().subsec_nanos() which could produce predictable sequences in tight loops. Adequate entropy in practice per distribution tests.

When total_weight is 0 (all proxies failed but not bad), select_weighted_proxy() returns available[0]. Could fall back to round-robin instead. Edge case unlikely in practice since bad proxies are already excluded.

Fixed missing trailing newline in use-settings.ts (EOF without newline)

summary: All 4 proxy-health features passed review with no blocking issues. The implementation adds comprehensive health tracking (ProxyStats with success/failure counters), bad proxy detection (3 consecutive failures threshold), cooldown system (configurable 30-300s with lazy evaluation), and weighted rotation (cumulative weight distribution). Test coverage is strong: 162 Rust tests (77 new since proxy-core) and 167 frontend tests. TypeScript build errors remain pre-existing and non-blocking. Code quality is high across all features with consistent patterns. Non-blocking issues include lib.rs code duplication and minor edge cases in weighted rotation fallback behavior.
